| [OA-1](assumptions/OA-1.md) | (A1) | - | There is $\iota\in S_n$ with $\iota\sigma\iota^{-1}=\sigma^{-1}$, $\iota\tau\iota^{-1}=\tau^{-1}$ |

## CRIT — (Q2) criteria and settled cases

| id | old labels | status | summary |
|---|---|---|---|
| [CRIT-1](claims/CRIT-1.md) | R Prop 3.1 | Proved | For the p×q rectangle (PA-7) the unfolding is a torus with Λ=2pZ⊕2qZ; a class lies in C iff it has a primitive vector, so parity makes (Q1) fail for all (p,q)≠(1,1). |
| [CRIT-2](claims/CRIT-2.md) | R Rmk 3.2 | - | On a rectangle torus, x illuminates x+(2,0) along σ²; (Q1) fails only because it demands travel time of exactly one period. The argument that (Q2), not (Q1), is the right question. |
| [CRIT-3](claims/CRIT-3.md) | R Thm 5.1 | Proved | (Q2) holds at OA-0 if G is 2-transitive, G is abelian, some Christoffel value is an n-cycle, or G is normal and covered by conjugates of Christoffel cyclic subgroups. |
| [CRIT-4](claims/CRIT-4.md) | R Rmk 5.2 | - | Zmiaikou's threshold and the Aougab et al. list for the minimal stratum suggest the residual class is small; neither is used as an input, for four stated reasons. |
| [CRIT-5](claims/CRIT-5.md) | R Prop 5.3 | Proved | If some Christoffel value u is an n-cycle then (Q2) holds; geometrically, u is an n-cycle iff its direction is one-cylinder of height one. |
| [CRIT-6](claims/CRIT-6.md) | R Prop 5.4 | Proved | In the regular action g has cycle type \|g\|^(n/\|g\|), so a Christoffel value is an n-cycle iff it generates G; such a direction exists iff G is cyclic. |
| [CRIT-7](claims/CRIT-7.md) | R Cor 5.5 | Proved | G is an SL(2,Z)-orbit invariant, so the orbit of a normal origami with non-cyclic deck group has no single-cylinder representative; the one-cylinder route to (Q2) fails there. |
| [CRIT-8](claims/CRIT-8.md) | R Rmk 5.6 | - | A finite group is never the union of conjugates of one proper subgroup, so for a normal origami a single Christoffel direction meets all pairs only if it generates G. |
| [CRIT-9](claims/CRIT-9.md) | R Prop 5.7 | Proved | For a normal origami, (Q2) ⇔ every g≠1 is conjugate to a power of a Christoffel value. Worked with x, y, xy for the EW, D4 and 2×1 rectangle (that row is wrong: BOUND-3). |
| [CRIT-10](claims/CRIT-10.md) | R Fact 5.9 | - | Checked against Matheus's lectures: the Q8 origami with generators i, j is the EW (8 squares, H(1,1,1,1), genus 3); by CRIT-7 its orbit has no one-cylinder surface. |
| [CRIT-11](claims/CRIT-11.md) | R2 Prop 4.1 | Proved | Every G-orbital lies in one D_δ; R^pow meets each D_δ (δ≠0), and D_0 iff GA-D0; so (Q2) ⇔ each orbital is met. Under GA-EP with n>4, (Q1) fails (parity). |
| [CRIT-12](claims/CRIT-12.md) | R2 Thm 4.2 | Proved | Relative 2-transitivity GA-2T, together with GA-D0 when n>\|A\|, implies (Q2), with an explicit direction for each difference class. |
| [CRIT-13](claims/CRIT-13.md) | R2 Cor 4.3 | Proved | (a) Abelian G is regular, GA-2T, and (Q2) holds; under PA-6 this is exactly PA-7. (b) Under GA-EP, n>4, if the orbitals are the four ι-classes then (Q2) holds with K≤2. |
| [CRIT-14](claims/CRIT-14.md) | R2 Prop 4.4 | Proved | For 1≠T centralising G, gr(T) is one orbital of size n; it lies in R^pow iff some ⟨u⟩-orbit is T-invariant (odd orbit count suffices for involutions); and GA-2T fails if n>\|A\|. |
| [CRIT-15](claims/CRIT-15.md) | R2 Thm 4.5 | Proved | Under GA-EP and GA-HA: Λ=2Z², the orbitals are the ι-classes split only by graphs of centralising involutions, (Q2) ⇔ GA-CT, and (Q2) holds with K≤2 if C(G)=1. |
| [CRIT-16](claims/CRIT-16.md) | R2 Rmk 4.6 | - | Under GA-HA, orbitals refining the ι-classes are exactly graphs of centralising involutions; under PA-6 these come from at most three symmetries of P with half-integer axis/centre. |
| [CRIT-17](claims/CRIT-17.md) | R2 Thm 4.7 | Proved | GA-2T′ holds for abelian G, under GA-2T, or under GA-EP∧GA-HA; under GA-2T′, (Q2) ⇔ GA-CT′; GA-CT′ is necessary for (Q2) with no hypothesis. Recovers CRIT-12 and CRIT-15. |
| [CRIT-18](claims/CRIT-18.md) | R2 Lemma 4.8 | Proved | For a G-invariant block system: if block-pair stabilisers are transitive on B×B′, (Q2) holds on the quotient origami, and each in-block orbital is met, then (Q2) holds for G. |
| [CRIT-19](claims/CRIT-19.md) | R2 Prop 5.1 | Proved | Under the reflection datum (RD6), m≥5: H^+⊇A_m iff H^+ is primitive with a 3-cycle; a corner type with a unique reflex vertex supplies the 3-cycle, giving GA-HA and CRIT-15. |
| [CRIT-20](claims/CRIT-20.md) | R2 Prop 6.1 | Reduced (Proved under PA-6; Reduced in general (to row segments of length ≤2)) | If θ reflects P in a vertical (horizontal) mid-line, σ (τ) has a T_θ-invariant orbit, so gr(T_θ) is met. | [OBS-18](claims/OBS-18.md) | W9b | - | Draft remark: for T with ι(T) = 0 no primitive direction is ≡ ι(T) mod 2, so the literal GA-CT clause is false; this happens at PA-4 but not under GA-HA; pipelines must test (CT′)(i). |
| [OBS-19](claims/OBS-19.md) | W5 | Not settled (draft; not yet through /verify-claim) | Draft: if M → M′ → T² and a pair of distinct squares of M′ is not in R^pow(M′), no pair over it is in R^pow(M). Also: at PA-4 the normal/quotient parity obstruction is always absent. |
| [OBS-20](claims/OBS-20.md) | W7 | Not settled (draft; not yet through /verify-claim) | Draft: translation automorphisms of a PA-4 garage exist only when PA-SC fails; for a regular garage cover with group D, (CT′)(i) holds for all deck elements iff folded-core monodromies cover D. |
| [OBS-21](claims/OBS-21.md) | W10 | Not settled (draft; not yet through /verify-claim) | Draft: for a non-normal garage cover P → P′, pairs in a common fibre within one K₄-copy have d = 0; if D₀ also has a pair in different fibres outside every gr(T), then GA-2T′ fails. |

## CEX — counterexamples

| id | old labels | status | summary |
|---|---|---|---|
| [CEX-1](claims/CEX-1.md) | N8 | Disproved (the (Q2) instance) | Two 24-square cyclic pillowcase covers at N=12 refute (Q2) at OA-3 (every corner marked): the orbitals gr(T^{±1}), T = i ↦ i+4, are met by no power of a Christoffel value. Not PA-4 (GEO-13). |
| [CEX-2](claims/CEX-2.md) | N9, [N8p] Thm A, [N8p] Thm B, [N8p] Cor 5.1, [N8p] Prop 1.3 | Proved | Christoffel values never lie in ker ψ, so a C^pow element realising T^{±1} is an even power g², g ∉ ker ψ; their column shifts are non-units of Z/6, so gr(T^{±1}) misses R^pow, at every base point. |
| [CEX-3](claims/CEX-3.md) | N22, G8 | Proved | The Cayley origami of Z/4⋊Z/4 (normal, 16 squares) fails (Q2) exactly on gr(T_E), E = a²b² central, as squares of elements outside the Frattini subgroup lie in {1,a²,b²}. OA-3, not PA-4. |
| [CEX-4](claims/CEX-4.md) | N23, G9 | Proved | Column form over (Z/2)² with σ an involution: (Q2) fails on gr(T_e) by OBS-4; OA-3 via explicit μ,ν; G ≅ (Z/4×Z/2)⋊Z/2 has an involution outside its Frattini subgroup, so G ≇ Z/4⋊Z/4. |
| [CEX-5](claims/CEX-5.md) | N24, G10 | Proved | The abelian pillowcase datum A_p = Z/2×Z/4, χ = y mod 2 fails (Q2) on gr(T_(1,0)) at OA-3 by OBS-4, is not PA-4, and an explicit relabelling makes it the transpose of O_16^a: not new. |

## BOUND — bounds on K and n

| id | old labels | status | summary |
|---|---|---|---|
| [BOUND-1](claims/BOUND-1.md) | R Conj 5.8, R §7 open item 2 | Disproved (by BOUND-2 (R2 Prop 7.1); the item's own label reads Not settled) | Conjectured that directions with \|p\|+\|q\|≤K give (Q2) under OA-3 for a small absolute K, on evidence of three n=8 examples; disproved by BOUND-2 (the 1×2^r rectangle needs K≥2^r+1). |
| [BOUND-2](claims/BOUND-2.md) | R2 Prop 7.1 | Proved (disproves BOUND-1) | Under PA-7 the 1×2^r rectangle needs K≥2^r+1, so no absolute K exists at any level; K≤p+q for a p×q rectangle, and K≤2 under GA-HA with trivial centraliser. |
| [BOUND-3](claims/BOUND-3.md) | N6 | Proved | In G=Z/4×Z/2 all directions of size ≤2 miss (2,1); direction (2,1), word xxy, reaches it, so K_min=3 and the K=2 covering row in CRIT-9's table is wrong. |
| [BOUND-4](claims/BOUND-4.md) | N21, G7 | Proved | If a fibration with Λ′⊆pZ² has a fibre-preserving centralising T≠1 with gr(T)⊄R^pow, then n≥16 at every level OA-0..OA-3; attained at OA-3 by O16^a (CEX-3). |

## COMP — computational foundations

| id | old labels | status | summary |
|---|---|---|---|
| [COMP-1](claims/COMP-1.md) | N1 | Not settled | Lower Christoffel words in the four sign quadrants represent each primitive class of F_2 once (cited); still open: (Q2) is GL(2,Z)-invariant, hence constant on a Teichmüller curve. |
| [COMP-2](claims/COMP-2.md) | N2 | Not settled | States (g1,g2) simultaneously conjugate by G (by G^+ under OA-3) have conjugate subtrees, so one per class leaves R^pow unchanged; states drop from \|G\|² to the class count. |
| [COMP-3](claims/COMP-3.md) | N4 | Not settled | Replacing Z/M by a finite abelian A and parity by a character χ with χ(a_j)=1 should give the abelian square-tiled surfaces; unproved, and the match with Wright's normalisation is open. |
| [COMP-4](claims/COMP-4.md) | N5 | Not settled | Restates three proved necessary conditions for the pipeline: each T≠1 in the centraliser acts as a power of some u on a ⟨u⟩-orbit; GA-D0 when n>\|A\|; every G-orbital is met. |
| [COMP-5](claims/COMP-5.md) | W8 | Not settled (draft; not yet through /verify-claim) | Sketch: for T of prime order, GA-CT′(i) fails iff the class of M→M/⟨T⟩ vanishes on every rational cylinder core; computable from cusp representatives without enumerating G. |
